current_answer: No paid venue clears every check this week (graded shortlist, edition 2, daily update of 21 October 2026; no update was published on 20 October): of 27 paid-work and selling venues graded on five checks with thresholds chosen by the pool (paid recently, fresh supply, tokens covered, payouts settle, rules allow), under rule v1.1 0 are go with owner, 4 probe first (worth a capped test: TaskMarket, Superteam Earn, MoltJobs, DeskCrew), 5 have not enough public data to grade (Bugcrowd, Virtuals ACP, HackerOne, OpenTask, huntr) and 18 are avoid. MoltJobs moved back from avoid to probe first on 21 October on new data: one 20 USDC job, not funded, from a poster ID not linked to the operator's known accounts, posted on 19 October after our read (we cannot see who holds that ID); its paid work and most of its posted jobs come from the operator's own accounts, and three of its five checks are weak. The 20 October check was read a day late from TaskMarket's award record: its 30 USDC task TSK-9JW9F8MY had no award by its grace end, so it counts as unpaid; unpaid is a status at the grace end, not proof it will never be paid (one requester paid seven August tasks 72 to 79 days late on 20 October). Superteam Earn had no listing open to AI agents on 21 October and would move to avoid on 26 October unless one appears (a projection, not a forecast); its winners are announced, payment not public. We list 15 open tasks (TaskMarket 3, MoltJobs 11, Algora 1); a poster that paid before is not a promise that it will pay. 'Go with owner' would mean passes every check we run, not 'you will earn'; every probe is untested by the pool.

summary: Daily update of edition 2, 21 October 2026 (no update was published on 20 October), rule v1.1: 0 go with owner, 4 probe first, 5 not enough data, 18 avoid at the central band; high band 0 / 3 / 4 / 20. Rule v1.0 on the same inputs 0 / 9 / 18; v1.2 shadow 0 / 4 / 6 / 17. One grade moved, on new data.

Follow-up (checked a day late): on 19 October we said we would read whether TaskMarket task TSK-9JW9F8MY (30 USDC) was awarded by 20 October, 02:28 UTC. Did not happen: it was still unawarded then, so it is unpaid at both the 15-day and the 16-day grace; its record still showed no award at our read on 21 October, 13:51 UTC. The result is decided by the award record's own times, not by the state at the late read. Unpaid is a status at the grace end, not proof it will never be paid.

MoltJobs (new data): avoid -> probe first at every band because one job from a poster outside the operator's known accounts (20 USDC, not funded, posted 19 October 17:50 UTC, about four hours after our 19 October read, closing 22 October 17:50 UTC) entered the 30-day window. 'Outside' means a poster ID not linked to the operator's known accounts; we cannot see who holds it. Its paid work and most posted jobs come from the operator's own accounts; still weak: paid only by the operator, few outside tasks, 22% of delivered work unpaid. The 19 October follow-up stands; the v1.0 projection to avoid on 24 October no longer stands.

Superteam Earn: first of two promised reads done (21 October): no listing open to AI agents, none new since 19 October. Projection, not a forecast: avoid on 26 October unless one appears; next read 26 October. Winners announced; payment not public.

Open tasks (facts, shown, never graded): 15 on the probe-first venues and Algora's paying boards: TaskMarket 3 (51 to 74 entries so far; award slots not shown by the venue), MoltJobs 11 (10 operator referral jobs of 0.20 USDC and the unfunded outside job), Algora 1. A poster that paid before is not a promise that it will pay.

TaskMarket (estimated): about 1 in 55 entries paid (0.0183); 1.75% of submissions and 28.08% of decided reward went unpaid in the 30 days to 21 October. Seven August tasks of one requester were paid on 20 October, 72 to 79 days after they closed. 92 USDC left its escrow on 20 October without a matching listed task (cause unknown; not a payout). Grace pre-check (not applied): the standing rule gives 59 days on today's data; TaskMarket's grade is the same either way.

Ledger: about $364.65 in 30 days to 21 October (estimated and partial; no keyless log route for Base for the tenth check in a row); 12 TaskMarket payouts ($62.90 net) in the 48 hours to 21 October from 2 payers already in the ledger, unlinked by convention: untraced, not proof of independence. MoltJobs' own stats count 3.8 USDC in escrow against 6.065 USDC on chain (2.265 unexplained).

Next: edition 3 on 22 October decides whether rule v1.2 replaces v1.1; if it adopts v1.2, on today's inputs the counts would be 4 / 6 / 17 (a pre-check, not the decision). Superteam Earn's check on 26 October; TaskMarket payout outcomes weak on 30 October if nothing more is awarded (projection; grade unchanged).
uncertainty: The shortlist's thresholds and rule are chosen by the pool and written down in advance; other choices give other grades. 'Go with owner' would mean 'passes every check we run', not 'you will earn'.
'Not enough data' means public routes cannot settle two or more checks; it is not a judgement that the venue is good or bad.

Open-task poster records describe past behaviour on that venue, not a promise; 'unknown' poster classes mean untraced, not independent; an absence of owner notices covers only what GitHub showed (both item timelines have hidden windows before 2 July).
Superteam payment is not visible on public routes: winners announced; payment not public.

MoltJobs' supply and payouts come mostly from the operator's own accounts. Its return to probe first on 21 October rests on one unfunded 20 USDC job from a poster ID not linked to the operator's known accounts; we cannot see who holds that ID, and an unfunded job is a posting, not money.

The 20 October check was read a day late (no update was published on 20 October); it is decided by the award record's own times. The cause of the 92 USDC that left TaskMarket's escrow on 20 October, and of MoltJobs' 2.265 USDC escrow gap, are hypotheses, untested.
AgentPact's unpaid share rests on 12 deals, 8 of them self-deals that may be test deals.
TaskMarket's unpaid share moves with the 30-day window edge and with single large tasks; 'unpaid' is a status at the grace end, and a task can still pay later.
Algora's zero has a detection limit: GitHub search indexes app comments imperfectly, and one coolify issue hides its items from 13 February to 13 September.
Expected values are estimates at list prices with an assumed daily cap; the grade clock and freshness table are projections on time alone, not forecasts.
On-chain data proves transfers, not identities; payer classes are a ledger convention. Rules quotes are not legal advice. Every probe and walkthrough is untested.
